method: Read every complete biography twice, including final corrected artifact. Checked disputed identities and key ship-role chronology against cited sources; this is an independent editorial/factual review, not a fresh archival reconstruction of every service date.
resolvedFindings: Ivanov-Nikolai: removed unsupported assertion that he personally resumed command and chose Qingdao. Gribovsky describes Shumov, then Matusevich, after Ivanov was wounded.
Ivanov-13: restored the actual relationship to Peresvet in 1916, without confusing it with his emergency command of Rurik in 1904.
Lyubinsky: unsupported Electric Cliff command assertion is absent; current profile stays within shipboard artillery role.
sourceChecks: Gribovsky, Tsesarevich: command succession, separate hits on bridge and conning tower, departure and internment.
Yalta Museum Gubonin family article with RGA VMF references: Pyotr Nikolayevich, grandson of Pyotr Ionovich, 1897 school application, wound and separate evacuation.
Bayan appendix: Aleksandr Rostislavovich Rodionov, 1849–1910, command 1899–1902, distinct from Viren's combat command.
Diana chapter 4: Brovtsyn's watch and detection of torpedo boats; Pallada repair chronology.
Diana chapter 6: Cherkassky's Saigon proposal, Lieven's decisions and Grozovoy/Brovtsyn route to Shanghai.
Peresvet chapter 4: Sarnavsky's temporary substitution for Zatsarenny.
Pobeda officer list: Lyubinsky senior gunnery officer, Wilken junior gunnery officer.
Biographical chronology crosschecks: Shter's Skory death, Dmitriev's temporary command, Cherkasov identity and brother, Uspensky postwar service, Ivanov-13's Peresvet command.
limits: Uncertain death years and disputed expanded patronymics remain explicitly unresolved rather than invented.
Several remaining service chronologies rely on identified reference biographies; no claim that all archive originals were examined.
